title: Measuring LLM Sycophancy under Sustained Multi-Turn Pressure
abstract: arXiv:2609.09090v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) may abandon correct positions when users push back, exhibiting a failure mode known as sycophancy. Existing evaluations typically use short, pre-specified conversations and may therefore miss failures that emerge under sustained, adaptive disagreement. We introduce SPINE, a benchmark in which an LLM proxy plays a persistent but mistaken user and adaptively challenges a target model for up to 25 turns. We evaluate four production systems and three Olmo3-7b variants on 100 false-presupposition and 100 unethical-query items. Our experimental results show that collapse rates increase with conversation length for every model, short-horizon protocols underestimate sycophancy and resistance under sustained pressure remains unreliable across current models. translated_title: 持续多轮压力下测量大语言模型的谄媚行为
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在用户反驳时可能放弃原本正确的立场，表现出一种被称为“谄媚”的失败模式。现有的评估通常使用简短的、预先设定的对话，因此可能遗漏在持续、适应性分歧下才显现的失败。我们提出了SPINE基准，其中一个LLM代理扮演一个固执但立场错误的用户，以适应性的方式对目标模型进行长达25轮的持续挑战。我们在100个虚假前提项目和100个不道德查询项目上评估了四个生产系统以及三个Olmo3-7b变体。实验结果表明：所有模型的崩溃率都随对话长度的增加而上升；短期评估协议会低估谄媚程度；且在持续压力下，现有模型的抵抗能力仍然不可靠。通过分析具有可访问推理轨迹的模型，我们惊讶地发现，即使在模型放弃正确立场时，正确答案往往仍然保留在推理轨迹之中。
tldr: 该论文提出SPINE基准，让一个LLM代理扮演固执而错误的用户对目标模型进行长达25轮的适应性挑战，揭示出谄媚崩溃率随对话长度增加而上升、短期评估协议会低估谄媚问题，且当前模型在持续压力下的抵抗力仍不可靠。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces SPINE, a benchmark where an LLM proxy plays a persistent but mistaken user and adaptively challenges target models for up to 25 turns, revealing that sycophancy collapse rates increase with conversation length, short-horizon protocols underestimate sycophancy, and resistance under sustained pressure remains unreliable across current models.
